title: The Beatles attempt to take ownership of Northern Songs | 1969
content:
On 11 April 1969 a formal offer was made by media company ATV to buy 1,604,750 shares in Northern Songs, the company which published much of The Beatles’ songwriting. On 20 April The Beatles made a counter offer.

ATV had increased their Northern Songs holdings from 137,000 to 1,741,750 shares, giving them almost 35% of Northern Songs.

Acting on behalf of The Beatles, Henry Ansbacher & Co made their offer to the company’s shareholders. They offered a higher price per share of 42 shillings and sixpence, significantly higher than ATV’s purchase price of 37 shillings.

In order to complete the deal and control the company, The Beatles needed to purchase 1.15 million shares at a total cost of £2.4 million. They needed to borrow £2 million, half of which was to come from investment company Henry Ansbacher.

ATV, however, were adamant that their shares were not for sale. “We have 35 per cent of the shares and they will stay with us,” its managing director Lew Grade told The Times newspaper.

The tussle over the company’s ownership prompted a number of broker firms to form an alliance known as the Consortium, which swiftly acquired a 14% stake in the company. As a result, ATV and The Beatles both needed the Consortium’s support in order to gain a controlling stake.

The Consortium was composed of three prominent London brokers: Astaire & Co, WI Carr, and Spencer Thornton. It represented clients including theatre owners Howard & Wyndham, the Ebor Unit Trust, the Slater Walker Investment Trust, and merchant bankers Arbuthnot Latham.

Although The Beatles’ business manager Allen Klein attempted to broker a deal with the Consortium, he was ultimately unsuccessful. Eventually, Grade called Peter Donald, a major shareholder in the Consortium, and offered 40 shillings per share for their holdings in Northern Songs. Although significantly less than The Beatles’ offer, Donald accepted. In September 1969 The Beatles lost control of the company, and Grade controlled 54% of Northern Songs.
